sentences.text: Probrachylophosaurus was a large quadrupedal hadrosaur featuring slender forelimbs, robust hindlimbs, and a long tail stiffened by ossified tendons.
Scientists estimate this dinosaur reached a total length of 10 meters.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, had an estimated body mass of 4.3 metric tonnes at death.
A defining feature was a short, paddle-shaped head crest formed by an extension of the nasal bone.
The dinosaur was first discovered in Montana in 1981 and fully excavated in 2008.
Probrachylophosaurus bergei was named and described in 2015 by Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler and Jack Horner.
In 2021, three specimens from the Foremost Formation were assigned to the genus Probrachylophosaurus but not to the species P. bergei.
Histologic analysis indicates that Probrachylophosaurus experienced fast growth rates similar to other hadrosaurs.
Comparisons with Maiasaura suggest Probrachylophosaurus took approximately twice as long to reach sexual maturity.
The oldest known specimen was approximately 14 years old and had reached over 95% of its adult size at death.
Probrachylophosaurus is classified as a hadrosaur within the solid-crested subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
Later phylogenetic analyses suggest Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus are close relatives, excluding Maiasaura from their immediate lineage.
Probrachylophosaurus, Brachylophosaurus, and Ornatops are united by a specific anatomy of the frontal and nasal sutures that supports a wide, backward-projecting head crest.
Fossils of Probrachylophosaurus date to the Campanian age between 80.45 and 79 million years ago.
Probrachylophosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 79 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
Brachylophosaurus goodwini is listed as a possible synonym for Probrachylophosaurus.
Some researchers suggest Brachylophosaurus goodwini might be a younger specimen of Probrachylophosaurus bergei, but poor preservation prevents a definite conclusion.
It is unknown whether Probrachylophosaurus exhibited variation between slender and robust crest morphologies between individuals, as seen in Brachylophosaurus.
Researchers suggest that Acristavus may have been the direct ancestor of Probrachylophosaurus, which in turn was the ancestor of Brachylophosaurus, which lived about 1.5 million years later.
